notes: This file records staged bring-up semantics conventions that are consumed by the Sail formal model and referenced by the manual.
These conventions are normative for v0.57. Rules not changed by the reviewed v0.57 delta are retained by v0.57.

regdst_writeback.description: Destination selector semantics for RegDst-like fields that can target GPRs or ClockHands pushes.

no_output.behavior: No architectural output is produced (silent drop). No exception is raised.

srcrtype.order: Apply SrcRType first, then apply any explicit shift (e.g. <<<shamt or <<shamt in addressing).
srcrtype.word_ops: For *W (32-bit) operations, apply modifiers at 32-bit width, compute a 32-bit result, then sign-extend to 64-bit.

restricted_forms.description: For forms whose assembly syntax only allows {.sw,.uw} (e.g. CMP.{EQ,NE,LT,GE,LTU,GEU} and SETC.{EQ,NE,LT,GE,LTU,GEU}), SrcRType=11 is treated as 00 (no modifier) in v0.57, retained by v0.57.

csel.description: CSEL encodes an optional .neg on SrcR; other SrcRType values are treated as 00.

setc_immediates.description: Immediate-compare conventions for SETC.*I forms with an encoded shamt field.
setc_immediates.encoding: SETC.*I encodes simm/uimm plus a 5-bit shamt (bits[11:7] in 32-bit forms, analogous position in HL forms).
setc_immediates.assembly: Assembly syntax elides shamt (prints a single immediate). Assembler/tooling may choose shamt to represent larger aligned constants when encodable.

pc_relative.base: current instruction PC (scalar blocks) or current instruction TPC (vec bodies); the instruction description says PC/TPC.

addtpc.note: ADDTPC uses a signed immediate (addtpc simm).

setret.note: SETRET uses an unsigned immediate (setret uimm).

fused_bstart_call.description: The exact 32-bit and 48-bit BSTART.CALL forms embed a call transfer and C.SETRET. Their adjacent immediate fields remain independent operands.
fused_bstart_call.operand_rule: simm12/simm25 and uimm5 are independently relocatable PC-relative operands; they MUST NOT be concatenated into one target.
fused_bstart_call.p_definition: P is the address of the first byte of the fused form.

division.description: DIV/REM family conventions (v0.57, retained by v0.57).

word_writeback.description: For *W variants, compute in 32-bit domain then sign-extend result to 64-bit.

multiplication.description: MUL family conventions (v0.57, retained by v0.57).

scalar.note: Scalar MUL/MULU return the low 64 bits of the full product.

word_writeback.description: For *W variants, compute in 32-bit domain then sign-extend result to 64-bit.

hl_two_dest.description: HL.MUL/HL.MULU return the full 128-bit product split across two destinations.

hl_madd.description: HL.MADD/HL.MADDW return a 128-bit accumulator split across two destinations.

block_legality.description: Legality conventions for which instruction families may appear as payload in coupled scalar blocks vs engine bodies.

bru_control_transfer.description: BRU control-transfer instructions (B.* / J / JR / etc.) are not legal payload in coupled scalar blocks; they are vec-engine scalar-lane-only.

on_scalar_block_execute.name: ILLEGAL_INST
on_scalar_block_execute.note: v0.57 requires a precise illegal-instruction trap with TRAPARG0 set to the offending scalar-block PC/TPC; this rule is retained by v0.57.

pc_relative.jr_srczero: The encoded SrcZero field is ignored (treated as 0) in v0.57, retained by v0.57.
pc_relative.jr_alignment: No forced alignment; odd target is permitted (subsequent fetch may fault).

tpc_misalignment_fault.name: BLOCK_TRAP
tpc_misalignment_fault.note: Use E_BLOCK(EC_BFETCH) for non-MMU body fetch faults (alignment).

tpc_invalid_target_fault.name: BLOCK_TRAP
tpc_invalid_target_fault.note: Vec-engine BRU targets that are outside the vec-body fetchable region (or otherwise not fetchable) are treated as body-fetch faults (not CFI).

body_range.note: The fetchable body region starts at BodyTPC and spans the compiler-authored out-of-line body selected by `B.TEXT`. `BSTOP`/`C.BSTOP` and `BSTART.*`/`C.BSTART.*` remain legal body terminators when control reaches them, but an earlier lexical terminator does not by itself truncate the body if group-internal control flow branches to a later label in the same body. Targets that escape the current `B.TEXT` body region fault as `E_BLOCK(EC_BFETCH)`.

predicate_register.name: p
predicate_register.truth_rule: B.NZ taken iff p != 0; B.Z taken iff p == 0
predicate_register.vector_predication: vector instructions are implicitly predicated by p
predicate_register.note: Within canonical MPAR/MSEQ kernel bodies, p is a normal scalar-uniform source/destination register representing EXEC state.

register_domain.description: Vec engine scalar-lane BRU reads operands from the scalar-lane GPR file (not ClockHands queues).

contract_summary: Scope: vec-engine scalar-lane only (illegal in coupled scalar blocks => TRAPNUM=4 ILLEGAL_INST).
PC-relative scaling: offset is halfword-scaled (target = base + (sext(offset) << 1)).
JR: target = SrcL + (sext(simm12) << 1); SrcZero field ignored.
Predicate: B.Z/B.NZ test vec predicate register p (all-zero vs non-zero).
Faults: misaligned/unfetchable targets => E_BLOCK(EC_BFETCH), BI=1, TRAPARG0=faulting VA.
Body range: implicit/operational (no explicit architectural [BodyTPC,BodyEnd) boundary).
Operand registers: read scalar-lane GPR domain (not ClockHands).
vec_engine_scalar_lane.note: When executed in the vec engine scalar lane, BRU control-transfer updates the body-local TPC (not architectural global PC).

bitfields.description: Bitfield operations (BXS/BXU/CLZ/CTZ/BCNT/BIC/BIS/REV) parameter mapping and wrap-around semantics.
bitfields.wrap_around: Bit ranges are defined on a 64-bit ring. For i=0..N-1, field[i] = SrcL[(M + i) mod 64]. Equivalent: field = ROR64(SrcL, M) & mask_low(N).

alias.ROR: Alias of BXU with Nminus1=63 (N=64): ROR64(SrcL, M).

rev.description: REV performs byte-order reversal on the selected bitfield.
rev.operation: field = bitfield_wrap(SrcL, M, N); if (N % 8) != 0 then result=0 else reverse byte order of low N bits; high bits are zero.
rev.invalid_n: If N is not a multiple of 8, the result is 0 (silent).

prefetch.description: Prefetch / cache hint instructions (PRF/PRFI and HL variants).
prefetch.note: Scalar PRF/PRFI prefetch provides a non-faulting performance hint in v0.57. This rule does not apply to BSTART.TPREFETCH, which is a destination-free TLOAD and retains TLOAD faults.

floating_point_compare.description: Scalar floating-point compare conventions (FEQ/FLT/FGE and S-variants).
floating_point_compare.s_variants: modeled as aliases (no FP exception signaling modeled in staged Sail)

minmax.nan_behavior: maxNum/minNum (one NaN => other; both NaN => canonical qNaN)

signed_zero.fmax: when both inputs are zeros, return +0
signed_zero.fmin: when both inputs are zeros, return -0 iff any input is -0

fixup_blocks.description: Unmanaged fixup block routing rules (v0.57, retained by v0.57).

unmanaged_fixup_block.definition: BSTART.SYS FALL<, fixup_label (SYS block with explicit fixup_label)

exception_routing.when: synchronous exception occurs while executing inside an unmanaged fixup block
exception_routing.fault_visibility: precise to instruction: all prior instructions commit; faulting instruction has no architectural side effects

assert.cause_note: TRAPNO.CAUSE is populated; for ASSERT_FAIL it is fixed to 0.

masking.when_disabled: ASSERT is treated as NOP (no trap, no trap-envelope update)
masking.scope: ASSERT-instruction-generated ASSERT_FAIL only (other synchronous exceptions are unaffected)

template_integrity_fail.acre_continuation: ACRE RRAT_RESTORE and RRAT_DEFAULT both raise E_INST(EC_PARAM) in the manager for the fail-stopped source

frame_templates_r975.source_contract: R975 Template Fatal-State and Canonical Identity Contract

legality.fret_stk_target: fixed R10 restored from slot zero

fret_stk_stack_slot_zero.device_mmio_or_mixed_or_non_idempotent: phase_zero E_DATA/MMU_PERM before any cache, fabric, device, or MMIO physical read

phase_one_recoverable.acre_restore: retry exactly saved event; do not reissue VLOAD, reacquire lease, or repeat earlier events

validation_rows.VLOAD: normal ROB/IQ/LIQ/LSU precise data-fault owner with no rename destination
validation_rows.VTGT: normal ROB/block-control target row with owned translation and I-cache request

d3_ownership.successful_validation_retirement: validation rows may complete but retire only in the event-zero seal transaction

vload.eligible_memory: complete eight-byte Normal and explicitly idempotent

seal_and_recovery.before_seal_invalidation: wins and cancels phase zero with no effect
seal_and_recovery.after_seal_invalidation: lease wins; producer completion waits through traps, ACRE, suspension, FINAL, or fatal release
seal_and_recovery.rollback_after_seal: forbidden for SP, GPR, memory, target, progress, and trace effects
seal_and_recovery.final: qualifies full token, performs boundary transfer/retirement, and releases lease atomically
seal_and_recovery.lease_directory_suspend_rule: lease directory retains discoverability during suspension; a manager must resume through FINAL or choose fatal abandonment and cannot wait on its own deferred invalidation

template_integrity_fail.release_ack: one RELEASED_AFTER_ABORT per pending matching invalidation after quiescence
fatal_teardown_order: stop source-context issue, commit, wakeup, redirect, FINAL transfer, and new lease acquisition
snapshot exact envelope, state, owner, token, and pending transactions
advance template, row, and load generations
cancel every uncommitted row and request
invalidate VLOAD data, VTGT proof, token, and queued transfer
obtain quiescence from every listed owner before releasing the lease
atomically release the lease and create one RELEASED_AFTER_ABORT per pending matching invalidation
publish the fatal record for managing-ring inspection

template_owner_id.equality: all fields participate; mismatch is never alias
template_owner_id.reuse_rule: advance applicable ROBID wrap or template/row/LSID/load/store generation before numeric reuse

status_rules: matching post-seal transactions independently record DEFERRED_ACTIVE
FINAL creates one RELEASED_AFTER_FINAL per pending match
fatal release creates one RELEASED_AFTER_ABORT per pending match
post-release admission performs a new lookup at new directory generation
invalidation.stale_ack_rule: wrong producer, sequence, operation/scope, match, directory, owner, or status-generation is rejected; identical terminal AckID retransmission is idempotent
invalidation.physical_sharing_rule: physical lookup/cancel/drain/release work may be shared only for transactions matching the same exact LeaseID; producer transaction bases, status, and AckID remain independent
admission_rules: an admitted transaction cannot be dropped
an admitted matching transaction cannot complete before FINAL or fatal release
a manager cannot roll back or wait on its own deferred invalidation
terminal_rules: NO_MATCH after lookup at the transaction directory generation for nonmatches
CANCELED_PRE_EVENT only after cancellation prevents stale event-zero seal
DEFERRED_ACTIVE recorded independently for each post-seal match and is nonterminal
RELEASED_AFTER_FINAL created atomically by FINAL per pending match
RELEASED_AFTER_ABORT created atomically by fatal release per pending match after quiescence
post-release admission performs a new lookup at the new directory generation and normally receives NO_MATCH

target_proof.coherent_marker_provenance_cache: legal only when it proves the same target marker bytes, address-space state, code-visibility epoch, and invalidation scope as an actual current marker proof
target_proof.deferred_demand_paging: qualified only while every FRET effect remains withheld
target_proof.fault_owner: VTGT owns translation, execute-permission, marker, and CFI faults
